raw_response:
I have farmed long enough to know that at my age, on 12 mu with only two people in the household, I need a plan that is stable, not flashy. I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is what fits my fields, my irrigation, and my experience in Quzhou County. Wheat and maize are familiar, mechanizable, and lower-risk for me than trying to push too much cotton. I will still keep a small cotton area because it spreads risk and gives me some cash income, but I will not let cotton take over the farm because it needs more field watching and more pesticide work.

For wheat, I will use improved seed, put fertilizer on at a moderate but reliable level, and irrigate enough to protect yield because I have well water and I do not want to gamble on rainfall. For summer maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed and keep management simple and timely, with good nitrogen and two irrigations if rainfall is short. For cotton, I will plant only a smaller area, use better seed, keep potassium a bit higher, and accept that it needs more pesticide sprays. I am choosing steady yields and manageable labor over chasing the absolute highest output.
